Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
Observed start/menu: PEAK main menu offered Host Game, Join Game, Play Offline, Settings, Credits, Quit. Clicking Play Offline caused a brief black loading screen, then a first-person airport session. Whether this is a tutorial is unconfirmed.

Controls/mechanics observed: W moves forward; S backs up; A/D strafe; Left/Right arrow keys rotate the view. W+Shift was used for forward movement, but a speed/sprint effect was not verified. E picked up a highlighted white chess QUEEN from its pedestal; it disappeared and a pale icon appeared in inventory slot 2. Passport was selected in slot 1 throughout later observations. The passport displayed an ‘open’ prompt with a right-mouse icon, but pressing K caused no visible change, so the actual open control and passport purpose remain unresolved. Slot 2 later appeared empty; what happened to the queen is unknown. Several duplicate movement inputs were rejected for observation_age_limit and did not execute.

Observed airport layout/navigation: Initial central moving walkway led toward a departures display and an overhead ‘Gate 7 Departure ->’ sign. At the walkway’s end, the signed route was to the right. That side contains windows, a chessboard/pedestals, palms, leisure/pool flooring, planters, and mesh barriers. The window-side and pool-side mesh-wall routes were dead ends. A building beside the pool had repeated ‘GATE 7 NOW BOARDING’ signs; a boarding-looking kiosk and rope queue were visible across/near the pool, but were never reached or interacted with. Bushes, palms, planters, queue furniture, and walls repeatedly obstructed direct approaches. Backing away with S and using open tiled/pool flooring helped clear some snags. A nearby basketball-court area contains a ball rack and a large BING Airlines display. From there, an open corridor to the left had hanging blue signs and a distant blue kiosk. Latest documented scene before the final completed left turn was that corridor area; exact final orientation is uncertain.

Failed approaches: Following the signed right-hand route led through the chess/leisure area rather than directly to boarding. Repeated short left/right turns and forward/diagonal movement around the Gate 7 planters produced circling and obstructions, eventually pressing against a mesh fence/yellow barrier. No kiosk prompt, boarding interaction, passport inspection, or departure occurred. The distant blue/white booths and BING display have not been inspected closely; their functions are guesses only.

Active goal/unresolved hypotheses: Reach and interact with the Gate 7 kiosk/queue to board. The visible kiosk beneath NOW BOARDING signs is the strongest observed target; it is only a hypothesis that it triggers boarding. Use known open corridors/flooring rather than the confirmed mesh-wall dead ends. Unknowns include whether the passport must be opened/presented, whether the queen had any purpose, and whether the other blue kiosks provide directions or boarding.
